title: The Next-Up Line
eyebrow: You answered; this is the change going in

actions.fyi: Nothing needed. You already made the call: the line says what the agent is about to do, not what the work list says.

content.label: What changes at the top of every page
content.lead: One line, on every report you open.

rows: The name of a stage — "Build it"
The thing about to happen, in the agent's words
The work list, and only that
The plan the agent already wrote at the bottom of the page
When the work list is behind
The line says nothing has started
The line still says what is coming
Unchanged — still the work list's answer

blocks.label: Why the list stays as it is
blocks.text: The tick list is the one part of a page nobody writes, so it is the one part that cannot flatter. Leaving it alone is what keeps the page something you can hold an agent to.

rows.title: A page whose agent wrote no plan
rows.note: It falls back to the work list, exactly as today, and reads as a stage name again. Nothing stops an agent leaving the plan empty; if that turns out to be common, the builder can refuse it, but no page here does that today.

rows.title: A job with nothing left
rows.note: It keeps the work list's own last word — everything is finished — rather than advertising a plan step under a full set of ticks.

rows.title: Pages that went stale before today
rows.note: The refusal that landed this morning keeps a page and its list moving together from now on. It does not go back and mend the ones already adrift; those mend the next time someone touches their job.

decisions.title: The next-up line comes from the agent's plan, not the work list
decisions.why: Your words: take the next-up line from what the agent wrote, not from the work list. The line is the first thing you read and it was the least true thing on the page.

decisions.title: The line names the step the plan is starting on
decisions.why: A plan marks whichever step is being started. That is what is happening next; the rest are further down the same page.

decisions.title: The now line and the tick list stay the work list's answer
decisions.why: You asked about next-up only, and the value of the rest is that no agent writes it.

next.if_nothing: It goes in as described, and you see it on the next page you open.

steps.step: Someone who did not write it reads it, then it lands
